title: Machine-learning analysis identifies a plasma protein signature associated with ALS years before symptoms
summary: In a plasma-proteomics study, machine learning selected a 17-protein panel from 33 proteins that differed between 183 people with ALS and 309 controls. The panel distinguished ALS from healthy participants and other neurological diseases in a held-out test set (AUC 96.2%, balanced accuracy 89.3%) and was assessed in independent cohorts, including UK Biobank samples. Applying the model to presymptomatic samples from people who later developed ALS showed risk-score shifts up to about 10 years before symptom onset.
ai_technology: Machine-learning classification model trained on Olink plasma proteomic features
organization: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke and collaborating ALS registry and research institutions

evidence.tested: The panel distinguished ALS from healthy participants and other neurological diseases in a held-out test set (AUC 96.2%, balanced accuracy 89.3%) and was assessed in independent cohorts, including UK Biobank samples.
evidence.unknown: This is a candidate biomarker result, not a clinically available diagnostic or screening test. The discovery and neurological-disease test cohorts are modest; the presymptomatic analysis is retrospective, and broader ancestry representation and prospective longitudinal validation remain needed. The paper reports multiple cohort-specific metrics; the summary uses the detailed held-out test-set AUC and balanced accuracy rather than the abstract’s 98.3% model figure.
evidence.ai_role: The model selected a multiplex protein signature and classified ALS versus healthy and neurological-disease controls; the researchers then applied its risk score to presymptomatic samples to estimate disease-associated changes before onset.
